summary: The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints teaches in its Articles of Faith that a person must be called of God by prophecy and by the laying on of hands by those in authority, and that the church has the same organization as the primitive church: apostles, prophets, pastors, teachers and evangelists. Its Gospel Topics page on priesthood says priesthood authority was lost after the first apostles and restored to Joseph Smith, that the senior living Apostle, the President of the Church, alone exercises all priesthood keys, and quotes M. Russell Ballard that men "have the unique responsibility to administer the priesthood", while men and women have "different but equally valued roles".

points.question: How is the church governed?
points.answer: The church has the same organization as the primitive church, with apostles, prophets, pastors, teachers and evangelists. The President of the Church, the senior Apostle, is the only person authorized to exercise all priesthood keys.

points.question: Who may hold the priesthood?
points.answer: The page quotes M. Russell Ballard: men "have the unique responsibility to administer the priesthood, but they are not the priesthood". It says men and women have "different but equally valued roles", and that a husband presides in the family "with his wife as an equal partner".
